notes: Summary: mid-market product team—starting on hosted API, POC good, now a Dedicated conversation focused on predictable unit cost and burst behavior.
POC takeaways: chat latency acceptable (95th ~85ms) but embedding throughput needs tuning for bulk reindex jobs.
Commit ask (from Greenthread finance): want 12-month commit but prefer quarterly ramp to align with ARR; target ARR $200-300k.
Burst requirement: must support 2.5x baseline for 30 min windows during launches; ask for explicit burst bucket and predictable pricing for bursts.
Overage: customer asks for hard cap on overage unit price (max +30% over committed unit rate) and monthly invoice visibility.
Ramp schedule: proposed by SE - Q1 25% baseline, Q2 50%, Q3 75%, Q4 100% of committed capacity. Greenthread prefers front-loaded ramp (50% by Q2) to support roadmap.
Security: legal flagged data residency for EU customers (have EU tenants) — will need region pinning or Private later. KMS support mandatory.
Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'We like Redwood's throughput and tooling; we just need a predictable bill and a sensible burst/overage model.'
Integration notes: will integrate with Segment and internal event pipeline; need S3-compatible logs export + 90-day request logs for auditing.
Operational expectations: want canary deploys, silent-failover to hosted model variant, and tracing hooks into their APM (Datadog).
Drive refs: pricing deck v2 contains three commit bands (S/M/L), burst add-on, and ramp discount schedule. Security doc lists required contract clauses.
Next exec ask: CFO wants an alternate proposal that reduces up-front commit by 25% in exchange for a 6% price premium on baseline unit.
Blocker detail: legal needs Redwood's DPA + data residency language revised; procurement will not sign until overage cap agreed.
Jira notes: INF-2142 opened to confirm KV cache persistence across restarts; SEC-3371 tracks KMS key exchange playbook.
Short form call notes: 'AE: push flexible ramp; SE: recommend commit + burst bucket; CFO: wants annual commit with quarterly checkpoints.'
